services.name: Hwange Agro Inputs
services.notes: Hwange is primarily a coal-mining and tourism area. Limited commercial farming. This dealer stocks drought-tolerant sorghum, millet, and short-season maize for communal farmers. Livestock inputs are the main line — dips, vaccines for the significant cattle population.

services.name: Lupane Agro Supplies
services.notes: Main input dealer for Lupane district. Drought-tolerant varieties a priority — SC403 short-season maize, SDMV sorghum, Pearl millet. Also stocks traditional seed through community seed bank partnerships. Cotton seed for Cottco contract farmers in lower Lupane.

services.name: Tsholotsho Agro Dealer
services.notes: Tsholotsho is one of the drier districts in Matabeleland North. Pearl millet and sorghum are the primary crops. Sandy soils — groundnuts also important. Very limited input range compared to Bulawayo — plan ahead and stock up from Bulawayo at season start.

services.name: Nyamandlovu Agro Dealer — Umguza
services.notes: Umguza is the most agriculturally productive district in Matabeleland North — reasonable rainfall and proximity to Bulawayo. Supports more intensive farming including vegetables and groundnuts. Close to Bulawayo for supplementary inputs.

services.name: GMB — Lupane Depot
services.notes: Main GMB for Matabeleland North. Accepts sorghum, millet, and maize. Small volumes in most years given drought conditions. Also used as a distribution point for GMB subsidised grain in food insecure years. Register seller number before harvest.

services.name: GMB — Hwange Collection Point
services.notes: Seasonal GMB collection. Very low volumes in Hwange — most food security grain comes in rather than going out. Important in good rainfall years for small grain sales.

services.name: Hwange Town Market
services.notes: Hwange town market. Serves mine workers and tourism employees. Good demand for fresh vegetables — most supplied from Bulawayo. Local sorghum grain and groundnuts sell at this market. Tourism from Hwange National Park supports some demand for fresh produce at lodges.

services.name: Lupane Livestock Auction
services.address: Lupane Cattle Sales, Lupane Growth Point
services.open_hours: Bi-monthly auction — first and third Friday of month
services.notes: Primary livestock auction for Matabeleland North. Cattle are the dominant livelihood asset in this region. Bi-monthly auctions. Cattle from Lupane, Nkayi, Tsholotsho, and Binga all come here. Prices often lower than Bulawayo — consider transport costs before deciding where to sell.

services.name: Binga Fishing Market — Lake Kariba
services.open_hours: Daily at dawn and dusk (fish landing times)
services.notes: Kapenta and bream fishing is the primary income for Binga (Tonga) communities on Lake Kariba. Fish dried and transported to Bulawayo and Harare markets. Not a crop market — included for Binga district completeness. Sorghum and millet from communal plots sold informally near the harbour.

services.name: AGRITEX Provincial Office — Matabeleland North
services.notes: Provincial AGRITEX HQ for Matabeleland North. Coordinates 7 district offices. Given the severe drought-proneness of this province, the primary mandate is food security crop promotion, Conservation Agriculture, and livestock management. Government input scheme allocation also managed here.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Binga
services.notes: Binga is among Zimbabwe's poorest and most food-insecure districts. Ward officers focus on small grain production for household food security. Sorghum, millet, and traditional crops including nyimo beans are the priority. Moringa promoted for nutrition. Government food aid coordination is a major function of this office.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Bubi
services.address: District Agricultural Office, Bubi Growth Point
services.notes: Bubi has slightly better conditions than other Matabeleland North districts — some cotton and maize possible in good years. Ward officers advise on cotton agronomy and drought-resilient practices.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Lupane
services.notes: Lupane district has received significant NGO investment in food security and small grain promotion. AGRITEX works with Welthungerhilfe, FAO, and World Food Programme in this district. Key contact for NGO-supported seed distribution. Cotton in lower Lupane, small grains in upper areas.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Nkayi
services.address: District Agricultural Office, Nkayi Growth Point
services.notes: Nkayi is a cattle-dominant district with limited arable potential. Ward officers focus on small grain security and livestock management. Cotton is grown when rains permit. Community seed banks have been established by NGOs — ask AGRITEX for current contacts.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Tsholotsho
services.address: District Agricultural Office, Tsholotsho Growth Point
services.notes: Tsholotsho has sandy soils and limited rainfall — pearl millet and sorghum are the most reliable crops. Groundnuts grow well in sandy conditions. Conservation Agriculture with mulching has improved yields. Ward officers advise on timeliness of planting — critical in dry areas.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Umguza (Nyamandlovu)
services.notes: Umguza is the most productive district in Matabeleland North — proximity to Bulawayo and better rainfall. Ward officers advise on vegetable production, maize, and groundnuts for Bulawayo market supply. Some dairy farming also occurs here.

services.name: Agribank Zimbabwe — Hwange Branch
services.notes: Agribank Hwange. Limited agricultural lending compared to other provinces due to the difficult farming environment. Livestock loans are the primary agricultural product. Crop loans available for Umguza and Lupane where farming is more viable. Contact Bulawayo branch for larger facilities.

services.name: Matabeleland North Community Seed Bank Network
services.address: c/o AGRITEX Lupane, Lupane Growth Point
services.notes: Network of community seed banks established with NGO support (FAO, Welthungerhilfe) across Matabeleland North. Banks hold locally-adapted drought-tolerant varieties of sorghum, pearl millet, finger millet, cowpeas, and nyimo beans that are NOT available through commercial channels. Contact through AGRITEX Lupane to find your nearest seed bank. Access usually free or barter-based.
